correctness.rationale: For fixed \(\eta\), coefficient zeros are exactly preimages of one ray \([f^\perp]\) under the projective orbit map. In complex dimension two this is a single projective point. Every nonempty fiber has size \(|K|\,|\operatorname{Stab}_H([\eta])|=|G|/m(\eta)\), and \(f^\perp\) ranges over all rays, so the maximum zero proportion is exactly \(1/m(\eta)\). A finite faithful projective action on \(\mathbb{CP}^1\) has a ray with trivial stabilizer because each nonidentity element fixes at most two rays, proving \(p_0(\pi)=1/|H|\). Boundary cases \(H=\{1\}\) and \(m(\eta)=1\) are consistent.
